title: Tech Note: Manipulating Arrays, Strings, and Dates in 4th Dimension
author: Walt Nelson

historical_commentary.text: This note is a library/cookbook of reusable 4D language routines (array insert/delete/sort-navigation, date arithmetic, string padding/casing/formatting) built around the 'parameter indirection' (pointer) technique for writing generic, reusable procedures across multiple arrays or variables. The general utility-library approach and many individual algorithms remain conceptually valid, but 4D's language has since added many built-in equivalents (and object/collection-based alternatives) that reduce the need to hand-roll several of these routines, and the classic 4D Insider tool referenced for moving code between structures no longer exists in that form.
related_updates: 4D Insider, the standalone structure-documentation/code-transfer tool referenced for moving routines between databases, was long ago superseded by built-in project/methods management in the modern 4D IDE

Many of the manual string/date utility routines shown (e.g., custom padding, date arithmetic helpers) now have more direct built-in 4D language commands or object/collection methods available in modern 4D
'Parameter indirection' via pointers is still supported in 4D, though modern 4D code often favors object properties, collections, or named parameters for similar generic-routine goals
